source_text: Quoniam scriptum est et apostolicae disciplinae robustissima auctoritate firmatum. quia iustus ex fide uiuit, eaque fides officium a nobis exigit et cordis et linguae — ait enim apostolus: corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem — oportet nos esse et iustitiae memores et salutis, quandoquidem in sempiterna iustitia regnaturi a praesenti saeculo maligno salui fieri non possumus, nisi et nos ad salutem proximorum nitentes etiam ore profiteamur fidem, quam corde gestamus: quae fides ne fraudulentis calliditatibus haereticorum possit in nobis aliqua ex parte uiolari, pia cautaque uigilantia prouidendum est. est autem catholica fides in symbolo nota fidelibus memoriaeque mandata quanta res passa est breuitate sermonis: ut incipientibus atque lactantibus eis, qui in Christo renati sunt, nondum scripturarum diuinarum diligentissima et spiritali tractatione atque cognitione roboratis paucis uerbis credendum constitueretur, quod multis uerbis exponendum esset proficientibus et ad diuinam doctrinam certa humilitatis atque caritatis firmitate surgentibus. sub ipsis ergo uerbis paucis in symbolo constitutis plerique haeretici uenena sua occultare conati sunt: quibus restitit et resistit diuina misericordia per spiritales uiros, qui catholicam fidem non tantum in illis uerbis accipere et credere, sed etiam domino reuelante intellegere atque cognoscere meruerunt. scriptum est enim: nisi credideritis, non intellegetis. sed tractatio fidei ad muniendum symbolum ualet: non ut ipsa pro symbolo gratiam dei consequentibus memoriae mandanda et reddenda tradatur, sed ut illa, quae in symbolo retinentur, contra haereticorum insidias auctoritate catholica et munitiore defensione custodiat.
thought_title: Faith must be professed and defended
orientation: Augustine opens the treatise by explaining why the creed must be held in the heart, confessed with the mouth, and defended against heretics.
pass_a_gloss: Since it is written and established by the most robust authority of apostolic teaching that the just person lives by faith, and this faith demands from us the duty of both heart and tongue — for the apostle says: with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation — we ought to be mindful both of righteousness and of salvation, since, being about to reign in everlasting righteousness, we cannot be saved from the present wicked age unless we also, striving for the salvation of our neighbors, profess with the mouth the faith which we carry in the heart. And provision must be made with pious and careful vigilance that this faith cannot be violated in us in any part by the deceitful cunning of heretics. But the catholic faith is known to the faithful in the creed and committed to memory, in as great a matter as it has undergone with brevity of speech: so that for beginners and infants, those who have been reborn in Christ, not yet strengthened by the most diligent and spiritual treatment and knowledge of the divine scriptures, it was established that belief should be constituted in few words, which would have to be expounded in many words for those advancing and rising to divine teaching with the sure firmness of humility and love. Under those very few words established in the creed, many heretics have attempted to hide their poisons: against whom divine mercy has resisted and does resist through spiritual men, who have merited not only to receive and believe the catholic faith in those words, but also, with the Lord revealing, to understand and know it. For it is written: unless you believe, you will not understand. But the treatment of faith serves to fortify the creed: not so that it itself, instead of the creed, should be handed over to those following the grace of God to be committed to memory and rendered, but so that it may guard those things which are retained in the creed against the snares of heretics with catholic authority and a more fortified defense.

choices.why: Keeps the superlative force and the physical metaphor of strength that Augustine uses for apostolic teaching.
Saeculum here is the present world-age opposed to the coming reign; 'maligno' is rendered literally as 'wicked' rather than 'evil' to preserve the moral nuance.
Lactantibus literally means 'those being nursed' or 'sucklings'; 'infants' captures the metaphor of new Christians not yet on solid food.
The metaphor of poison for heretical teaching is vivid and should be kept literal.
Keeps the gendered Latin uiros and the adjective 'spiritual' as a quality of those who understand the faith.
The comparative munitiore continues the military metaphor of fortification begun with muniendum.

bible_refs.note: corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem

pass_b_english: Since it is written, and confirmed by the most robust authority of apostolic teaching, that the righteous person lives by faith, and since this faith demands from us the service of both heart and tongue—for the apostle says, "With the heart one believes and is justified, and with the mouth one confesses and is saved" (Romans 10:10)—we must be mindful of both righteousness and salvation. For we are destined to reign in everlasting righteousness, and we cannot be saved from this present wicked age unless we also strive for the salvation of our neighbors and profess with our mouth the faith we carry in our heart. We must take pious and careful watch that this faith cannot be violated in us in any part by the deceitful cunning of heretics.

Now the catholic faith is known to the faithful in the creed and committed to memory, in as brief a form of words as so great a matter allows. Its purpose is that for beginners and infants—those who have been reborn in Christ but are not yet strengthened by the most diligent and spiritual study and knowledge of the divine Scriptures—what they are to believe should be set down in few words, while for those advancing and rising to divine teaching with the firm foundation of humility and love, it would need to be expounded in many words. Under those very few words set down in the creed, many heretics have tried to hide their poisons. Divine mercy has resisted them, and still resists them, through spiritual men who have merited not only to receive and believe the catholic faith in those words, but also to understand and know it by the Lord's revelation. For it is written, "Unless you believe, you will not understand" (Isaiah 7:9).

But an exposition of the faith serves to fortify the creed—not so that it should be handed over in place of the creed to those who are attaining God's grace, to be memorized and recited, but so that the things held in the creed may be guarded against the snares of heretics by catholic authority and a more fortified defense.

problems.source_quote: Quoniam scriptum est et apostolicae disciplinae robustissima auctoritate firmatum. quia iustus ex fide uiuit
problems.why: Source cites apostolic authority, not Habakkuk; Paul cites Habakkuk but Augustine cites Paul here.
problems.fix: Remove (Habakkuk 2:4); the source attributes 'the righteous lives by faith' to apostolic teaching, not directly to Habakkuk.
problems.ruling: Source says 'scriptum est' and 'apostolicae...auctoritate'; Paul cites Habakkuk, but Augustine cites apostolic authority, not Habakkuk directly.

problems.quote: in place of the creed to those who are following God's grace
problems.source_quote: non ut ipsa pro symbolo gratiam dei consequentibus
problems.why: 'gratiam dei consequentibus' means 'to those obtaining/attaining God's grace,' not 'following God's grace'; 'consequentibus' is present participle of 'consequor'.
problems.fix: in place of the creed to those who are attaining God's grace
problems.ruling: 'consequentibus' = present participle of 'consequor' = 'obtaining/attaining'; 'following' mistranslates, changing meaning to pursuit not attainment.

edits.old: the righteous person lives by faith (Habakkuk 2:4)
edits.new: the righteous person lives by faith

edits.old: to those who are following God's grace
edits.new: to those who are attaining God's grace

fixed: Removed (Habakkuk 2:4): source attributes the quotation to apostolic teaching, not directly to Habakkuk.
Changed 'following God's grace' to 'attaining God's grace': 'gratiam dei consequentibus' means those obtaining/attaining God's grace.

last_rejected.quote: Unless you believe, you will not understand
last_rejected.why: This is Isaiah 7:9 in the Old Latin version (Septuagint-based). The standard Hebrew-based version has 'If you do not stand firm in faith, you shall not stand at all' (NRSV). The English correctly renders the Old Latin wording Augustine quotes, but the citation '(Isaiah 7:9)' should perhaps note the Septuagint difference per the brief. However, the brief says 'Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and, for Psalms, the Hebrew numbering with a note where the Septuagint numbering differs.' This is Isaiah, not Psalms, so no special note required. The English matches Augustine's quoted text. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly renders 'nisi credideritis, non intellegetis' and Isaiah 7:9 citation is standard; no error per brief.
